title: Settings + encrypted secrets
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

A Settings screen where the developer enters non-secret configuration (Jira base URL, Tempo host, Jira accountId, active repo path, Obsidian vault path, LLM model) and per-integration API tokens. Non-secret config persists in the settings table; tokens are stored through the Secret Store module backed by Electron safeStorage. All values survive a restart; tokens are never written to SQLite in plaintext.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings screen reads/writes non-secret config to the settings table
- [ ] API tokens are stored/retrieved via safeStorage (Secret Store), never in plaintext in the DB
- [ ] Config and tokens persist across an app restart
- [ ] Tokens can be updated/rotated from Settings

## Blocked by

Slice 2 — NSIS packaging + native module in installer
notes: TDD complete. 20 Vitest tests green (4 settings, 6 secret-store, 3 ipc, 3 db, 4 migrations). Schema migrations v2+v3 add settings+secrets tables. SafeStorageAdapter interface keeps tests Electron-free. Four IPC channels wired (settings:get/set, secrets:get/set). Build clean. GUI verification of safeStorage behavior on Windows pending.
close_reason: TDD complete: 20 tests green, build clean, migrations v2+v3, settings+secrets IPC wired. safeStorage behavior on Windows is HITL-only (same gate as o_g_a_r-uvy).

title: Walking skeleton + native SQLite
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Stand up the Electron shell with a React + shadcn/ui renderer (electron-vite), typed IPC over contextBridge/invoke (contextIsolation on, no nodeIntegration), an embedded SQLite database via better-sqlite3 that self-creates on first run, and a migration runner keyed on PRAGMA user_version. The renderer displays a value read from the migrated database over a typed IPC call, proving every layer connects end-to-end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] App launches in dev (electron-vite) with the renderer rendering a shadcn/ui component
- [ ] better-sqlite3 loads in the main process (native module rebuilt against the pinned Electron version) and opens a self-created .db file
- [ ] The migration runner applies migrations based on PRAGMA user_version and is idempotent across restarts
- [ ] A typed IPC channel returns a value read from SQLite, displayed in the renderer
- [ ] contextIsolation is enabled; the renderer has no direct Node access

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.
notes:
STATUS: code-complete, committed + pushed to master (commit 5b3f2d4). All verifiable gates green: 8 Vitest tests, tsc --noEmit, electron-vite build (main+preload+renderer bundle, Tailwind CSS emitted).

Implemented:
- Migration runner (PRAGMA user_version, ascending, idempotent, per-migration tx+rollback) — TDD 4 tests
- openDatabase()/readAppInfo() self-create+migrate, idempotent across restarts — TDD 3 tests
- Typed IPC contract src/shared/ipc.ts + registerIpcHandlers (narrow IpcRegistrar, electron-free unit) — TDD 1 test
- Electron shell: main opens DB + registers IPC; preload exposes window.ogar via contextBridge (contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off, sandbox off, strict CSP); React+Tailwind+shadcn Button renderer shows AppInfo over IPC
- README documents better-sqlite3 Node/Electron ABI dance (rebuild:electron / rebuild:node)

VERIFICATION GAP (env-blocked, app targets Windows; WSL Linux not representative + Electron-ABI rebuild would break Node test binary):
- GUI launch not run here. To verify+close: on Windows run 'npm run rebuild:electron' then 'npm run dev'; confirm window shows 'O.G.A.R.' + 'schema version 1' and the Refresh button works.

Acceptance criteria status: #2 self-creating db (tested), #3 migration idempotent across restarts (tested), #4 typed IPC value (tested + wired); #1 dev launch + shadcn component and #5 contextIsolation are coded+built but await GUI verification on Windows.
close_reason: Code complete: 8 Vitest tests green, tsc --noEmit clean, electron-vite build ok. Windows GUI launch gap documented in notes — HITL verification pending on Windows.

title: O.G.A.R. — Personal Dev-Productivity Hub & Tempo Worklog Assistant (PRD)
description:
# O.G.A.R. — Personal Dev-Productivity Hub & Tempo Worklog Assistant

> Private, local-first Electron desktop app (Windows) that helps a developer work on Jira tickets with a local LLM and report work time to Tempo. The name is a Polish acronym — *Osobisty Generator Asystencji i Raportów*. The product and all artifacts are in English.

## Problem Statement

As a developer, my day is split across Jira tickets, code, scattered notes, and Confluence docs — and at the end of it I have to reconstruct and log my time in Tempo, a tedious, error-prone chore I keep postponing and then rebuild from memory. The context I need to write a useful Jira comment or remember what I did (the ticket, my notes, my commits) is scattered across tools. I want help that runs entirely on my own machine, with no company data leaving it, and with no extra servers to install.

## Solution

O.G.A.R. acts on a single **active ticket** at a time. For that ticket it assembles a **Ticket Work Context** — the Jira issue, related Confluence pages (read-only), my Obsidian notes, and my Git changes — and feeds it to a **local LLM** (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama by default) to draft a Jira comment or a Tempo worklog description.

Every write is a human-approved **draft**: nothing is posted to Jira or Tempo without explicit confirmation. Time is captured by a lightweight Pomodoro timer (which ticket, how long) and corroborated by commits, so the developer can log Tempo the same day — or reconstruct a forgotten stretch from durable history. Tokens are encrypted via Electron `safeStorage`; all state lives in a single embedded SQLite file that self-creates on first run. Correctness of time logging is guaranteed by **reconciling against Tempo itself** — read-before-write to avoid duplicates, read-after-write to confirm.

## User Stories

**Setup & health**
1. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to create its own database on first run, so that I never install or configure a database server.
2. As a developer, I want a first-run settings screen collecting my Jira URL + token, Tempo host + token, my Jira `accountId`, my active repo path, my Obsidian vault path, and my LLM model, so that one guided setup gets me going.
3. As a developer, I want my API tokens stored encrypted via the OS secret store, so that credentials are never in plaintext.
4. As a developer, I want a startup check of my local LLM endpoint, so that I learn immediately if it isn't reachable.
5. As a developer, I want a clear message and a "re-check" action when the LLM endpoint is down (e.g., WSL port forwarding dropped after reboot), so that I know how to fix it instead of hitting silent failures.
6. As a developer, I want to pick my LLM model from the models actually installed locally, so that I'm not tied to a hardcoded name.
7. As a developer, I want to update my tokens and paths in settings at any time, so that I can fix or rotate credentials.

**Dashboard & active ticket**
8. As a developer, I want a dashboard listing my assigned tickets in the open sprint, so that I see my work at a glance on launch.
9. As a developer, I want to see how much time I've tracked so far today, so that I know where I stand before logging.
10. As a developer, I want to select a ticket as my active ticket, so that timing and assistance attach to the right work.
11. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to suggest the active ticket from my current Git branch when possible, so that I don't pick it manually every time.
12. As a developer, I want to change a ticket's status (e.g., to "Doing") from the dashboard, so that I keep Jira current without opening the browser.
13. As a developer, I want the offered status transitions to reflect the ticket's actual workflow state, so that I only see valid moves.

**Time capture**
14. As a developer, I want to start/stop a Pomodoro timer for my active ticket, so that time is captured against the right ticket.
15. As a developer, I want each finished session stored durably with ticket and start/end time, so that I can rebuild my day later if I forget to log.
16. As a developer, I want the timer to be a lightweight helper, not a strict discipline tool, so that it supports me without getting in the way.

**Notes & code as context**
17. As a developer, I want to keep per-ticket notes in my Obsidian vault and have O.G.A.R. read them by ticket, so that my in-flight thoughts feed the assistant.
18. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to find my commits for a ticket by the ticket key in the commit scope (e.g., `feature(ABC-123): ...`), so that my changes are attributed correctly regardless of branch name.
19. As a developer, I want both my committed and uncommitted changes for the active ticket included, so that the assistant sees what I actually did.

**Assistant**
20. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to assemble a Ticket Work Context (Jira issue + related Confluence + my notes + my Git changes), so that the LLM answers with full context.
21. As a developer, I want to ask the local LLM what I need to do on a ticket, so that I get oriented quickly.
22. As a developer, I want to manually pick or paste a specific Confluence page or Jira item as context, so that I can point the assistant at exactly the right material.
23. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to search Confluence/Jira by ticket key or terms and offer the top results as context, so that I don't hunt for them.
24. As a developer, I want large context sources capped or summarized to fit my local model's window, so that the assistant doesn't fail or truncate unpredictably.
25. As a developer, I want the assistant to read Confluence but never write to it, so that I never accidentally publish machine-generated docs.

**Jira comments**
26. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to draft a plain-text Jira comment from my changes and notes, so that I summarize completed work without writing from scratch.
27. As a developer, I want to edit the drafted comment before sending, so that I stay in control of what's posted.
28. As a developer, I want to regenerate the draft with a tweak (shorter, more formal), so that I refine it quickly.
29. As a developer, I want to explicitly approve a comment before it posts to Jira, so that nothing is published without my say-so.
30. As a developer, I want clear errors when posting fails (expired token, network), so that I can fix the cause and retry.

**Worklog & Tempo**
31. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to suggest today's worklog entries per ticket from my Pomodoro sessions, corroborated by commits, so that logging is mostly pre-filled.
32. As a developer, I want the LLM to draft each worklog's description from that day's commits and notes, so that entries are meaningful.
33. As a developer, I want durations rounded by a configurable rule (default 15 minutes), so that entries look clean.
34. As a developer, I want to manually add a worklog entry (ticket, time, description) for time not captured by Pomodoro (e.g., lunch, general meetings), so that my day adds up.
35. As a developer, I want to review and adjust the full set of worklog drafts before submitting, so that I can correct times and descriptions.
36. As a developer, I want to approve worklog submission explicitly, so that nothing is sent to Tempo automatically.
37. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to check Tempo for what's already logged that day before submitting, so that I never double-log time.
38. As a developer, I want O.G.A.R. to verify after submitting that my entries actually appeared in Tempo, so that I can trust the report went through.
39. As a developer, I want per-entry submission status (confirmed / failed) instead of all-or-nothing, so that I retry only what didn't go.
40. As a developer, I want to reconstruct and log a forgotten earlier period from my durable session and commit history, so that I can recover a week I forgot to log.

**Foundational**
41. As a developer, I want all data in a single local file with no external server, so that setup stays trivial and nothing leaves my machine.

## Implementation Decisions

**Shell & process model**
- Electron with a strict split: **main = orchestrator** (all API calls, Git, filesystem, DB, `safeStorage`); **renderer = UI only**.
- IPC is **typed**, over `contextBridge` + `ipcRenderer.invoke` / `ipcMain.handle`, with `contextIsolation: true` and no `nodeIntegration` in the renderer.

**Renderer stack**
- electron-vite + React + TypeScript + **shadcn/ui** (which brings Radix UI primitives + Tailwind CSS; components are copied in, not an npm dependency) + TanStack Query as the data layer over IPC.

**LLM**
- Provider abstraction targets the **OpenAI-compatible API** (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/embeddings`) — not Ollama's native `/api/*` — so the local backend is swappable (Ollama default; LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM also fit). Ollama-native endpoints used only for non-standard needs (model listing/pull).
- **Local-only**: no external/cloud model calls. The abstraction exists to swap *local* engines, for privacy, not to reach the cloud.
- The LLM returns **markdown / structured output** (`response_format` where structure is needed). It never emits ADF or Confluence storage XHTML directly — format conversion is deterministic code, not the model.

**Context retrieval**
- Two tiers: **T0** = explicit manual selection / paste; **T1** = Atlassian-native search (JQL/CQL) returning top results. No semantic/vector search.
- **Context Assembler** applies **per-source budget caps**; prefers notes + diff; large Confluence pages are summarized before inclusion so the bundle fits a small local model's window.

**Data**
- Embedded **SQLite via better-sqlite3**, a single self-creating `.db` file. **Migration runner keyed on `PRAGMA user_version`** (no ORM).
- Core tables: `worklog_draft`, `work_session`, `assist_draft`, `ticket_cache` (key → numeric `issueId` + summary), `settings` (non-secret config).
- DB content is **plaintext**; only API tokens are encrypted, via `safeStorage`. At-rest protection is left to OS disk encryption.

**Worklog correctness (the crux)**
- Truth lives in Tempo, not in local state. Submission flow: **pre-check** — `GET` the day's Tempo worklogs for the author and reconcile against drafts to drop duplicates; **submit** the non-duplicates; **post-check** — `GET` again and confirm each intended entry appeared.
- `worklog_draft.status` exists for **UI only** (`draft → approved → submitted → confirmed | failed`); correctness comes from reconciliation, not from trusting local status across a crash. When a returned Tempo worklog id is available it makes the post-check exact; otherwise reconcile by fingerprint (ticket + date + author + duration).

**Integration surface**
- **Jira**: READ issues + available transitions; WRITE plain-text comment + status transition. Transitions are **dynamic** — `GET .../transitions` for the current state, then `POST .../transitions` with the chosen `transitionId` (never hardcode a status). Comment body sent as plain text (v2 endpoint) or wrapped in a minimal single-paragraph ADF document; auth is Basic `email:token`.
- **Tempo**: READ (for reconcile) + WRITE worklog. **Separate token and host** from Jira. Worklog creation needs the numeric Jira `issueId` (looked up from the ticket key and cached) and the author `accountId`.
- **Confluence**: **READ-only** — CQL search + fetch page text. No create/update.
- **Git**: READ via **shell-out to system `git`**. Ticket attribution by parsing the **commit scope** `type(ABC-123): ...` with regex `[A-Z]+-\d+`, liberal about the `type` word. Gathers a ticket's work via `git log --grep` + diff of those commits, plus the working-tree diff. **Single active repo**, selected in the UI.
- **Obsidian**: READ/WRITE vault `.md` files directly via `fs`, addressed by a ticket convention (filename / frontmatter / wikilink). No dependency on a running Obsidian instance.

**Trigger model**
- **On-demand only**: every assemble/draft/submit is an explicit, conscious developer action. No background or automatic behavior.

**Startup health**
- On launch, ping `GET /v1/models`. If unreachable (e.g., Ollama not started in WSL, or port forwarding dropped after reboot), surface a clear remediation + "re-check"; O.G.A.R. does not auto-spawn the engine.

**Modules (deep modules with simple, stable, testable interfaces)**
- **LLM Client** — `chat`, `listModels`, `health`; OpenAI-compatible backend.
- **Jira Client** — `getIssue`, `searchIssues(jql)`, `getTransitions`, `transition`, `addComment`.
- **Tempo Client** — `getWorklogs(author, dateRange)`, `createWorklog`.
- **Confluence Client** — `searchPages(cql)`, `getPageText(id)` (read-only).
- **Git Activity Reader** — `commitsForTicket`, `diffForTicket`, `workingDiff` (shell-out).
- **Ticket-Key Parser** — pure: commit scope → ticket key.
- **Obsidian Vault** — `readNotesForTicket`, `writeNote` (fs convention).
- **Context Assembler** — `assemble(ticketKey) → bundle`, including the per-source budgeter.
- **Worklog Draft Builder** — pure: `sessions + commits → per-ticket drafts`, with rounding.
- **Worklog Reconciler** — pure: dedupe pre-submit + verify post-submit (Tempo client injected).
- **Time Tracker** — Pomodoro start/stop → `work_session`, attribution to the active ticket.
- **Secret Store** — `safeStorage` wrapper (`get`/`set`).
- **Migration Runner** — steps migrations on `PRAGMA user_version`.
- **Repositories** — per-entity CRUD over better-sqlite3.

**Build & distribution**
- electron-builder → NSIS `.exe`. better-sqlite3 is a native module → **`@electron/rebuild`** against a **pinned Electron version**; proving the native rebuild produces a working installer is the first build task. No code signing, no auto-update.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert **external behavior, not implementation details** — given inputs to a module's interface, assert outputs/effects; never reach into internals.
- Modules to test (confirmed with the developer):
  - **Worklog Reconciler** — highest value: the double-logging guard. Pure logic with an injected Tempo client; cover "already logged today → skip", "partial overlap", "post-check confirms / flags missing".
  - **Worklog Draft Builder** — aggregation of sessions + commits per ticket per day, and the configurable rounding rule.
  - **Ticket-Key Parser** — commit scope → key across `feature/feat/fix/...` and malformed scopes.
  - **Context Assembler budgeter** — per-source caps / truncation / large-page summarization selection.
  - **Obsidian Vault** — ticket → file convention, read and write, against a temp directory.
  - **Migration Runner** — `user_version` stepping forward across versions on a throwaway DB.
- **API clients** (Jira / Tempo / Confluence / LLM): **contract tests** against mocked HTTP — assert request shape and response parsing (including the Tempo `issueId`/`accountId` correlation and the dynamic-transition flow), not live network calls.
- This is a greenfield repo with no prior test art; these tests establish the conventions.

## Out of Scope

- **Writing to Confluence** — Confluence is read-only.
- **Any background / automatic / proactive behavior** — all actions are explicitly user-initiated.
- **Semantic / vector search** over the knowledge base — retrieval is manual selection + Atlassian-native search only.
- **Integrations beyond** Jira, Tempo, Confluence (read), Git, Obsidian, and a local OpenAI-compatible LLM.
- **Multi-user / shared server / central database** — single user, single machine, no external server.
- **Code signing and auto-update.**
- **Encryption of the SQLite database contents** — only API tokens are encrypted (via `safeStorage`); disk-level at-rest protection is the OS's job.

## Further Notes

- **Privacy is a hard constraint**: ticket/Confluence content and code must never leave the machine. The local-only LLM design enforces this; the OpenAI-compatible abstraction is for swapping local engines, not for cloud access.
- **Two Atlassian wrinkles to budget for** in implementation: Tempo's separate token/host and its need for the numeric Jira `issueId` + author `accountId` (look up via Jira, then post to Tempo); and Jira Cloud comment bodies being ADF (wrap plain text in a minimal ADF doc, or use the v2 endpoint).
- **WSL2 networking is fragile**: port forwarding to `localhost:11434` can drop after reboot — the startup health-check must surface a clear fix rather than failing silently.
- **First build de-risks the native module**: the better-sqlite3 / `@electron/rebuild` / Electron-version chain is the most likely thing to break packaging, so a working installer is proven before feature work piles on.

title: Worklog Draft Builder
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

The Worklog Draft Builder aggregates a day's work_session entries (corroborated by commits where available) into suggested worklog drafts per ticket, applying a configurable rounding rule (default 15 minutes). The developer can build drafts for today or reconstruct an earlier period from durable history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sessions are aggregated per ticket per day into suggested worklog drafts
- [ ] A configurable rounding rule is applied (default 15 minutes)
- [ ] Drafts can be generated for a chosen date/range (reconstruct a forgotten period)
- [ ] Suggested drafts flow into the existing submit + reconcile path

## Blocked by

Slice 9 — Pomodoro time capture -> work session

title: Obsidian vault notes by ticket
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Read (and write) the developer's per-ticket notes directly from the Obsidian vault .md files (path from settings), addressed by a ticket convention (filename / frontmatter / wikilink), with no dependency on a running Obsidian instance. The active ticket's notes are shown and can be fed as context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Notes for a ticket are read from the vault by convention, with Obsidian closed
- [ ] A note can be written/updated for a ticket (wikilinks preserved as text)
- [ ] Works against a configurable vault path
- [ ] The active ticket's notes are visible in the UI

## Blocked by

Slice 11 — Git activity reader + ticket-key parser

title: Context Assembler (Ticket Work Context)
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

The Context Assembler builds a full Ticket Work Context for the active ticket by combining the Jira issue, related Confluence pages (CQL + manual pick), Obsidian notes, and Git changes into one bundle fed to the assistant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Assembler combines Jira + Confluence + Obsidian + Git for the active ticket into one bundle
- [ ] Related Confluence pages are found by CQL and/or added manually
- [ ] The assistant answers using the full assembled context

## Blocked by

Slice 15 — Assist: what should I do on this ticket

title: Pomodoro time capture -> work session
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

A lightweight Pomodoro timer in the renderer that the developer starts/stops for the active ticket; each finished session is stored durably in work_session (ticket, start, end). The dashboard shows time tracked so far today. The timer is a helper, not an enforcement tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Start/stop a Pomodoro attributes the session to the active ticket
- [ ] Each finished session persists in work_session with ticket + start/end
- [ ] Dashboard shows today's tracked time
- [ ] Sessions survive restarts (durable history)

## Blocked by

Slice 8 — Worklog reconcile + verify

title: Jira comment: edit + regenerate
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Before posting, the developer can edit the drafted comment and regenerate it with a tweak (e.g., shorter, more formal), iterating until satisfied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The draft comment is editable before posting
- [ ] Regenerate produces a revised draft from a tweak instruction
- [ ] The edited/regenerated text is what gets posted on approval

## Blocked by

Slice 18 — Jira comment: draft -> approve -> post

title: Git activity reader + ticket-key parser
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Point at the active repo (path from settings). The Ticket-Key Parser extracts the ticket key from the commit scope (type(ABC-123): ...) using [A-Z]+-\d+, liberal about the type word. The Git Activity Reader (shell-out to system git) gathers a ticket's commits via git log --grep plus their diffs and the working-tree diff. The UI shows the assembled code changes for the active ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ticket-Key Parser extracts the key from varied commit scopes and ignores malformed scopes
- [ ] Git Activity Reader returns commits + diffs for a ticket via shell-out, plus the working-tree diff
- [ ] A single active repo is configurable
- [ ] The active ticket's code changes are viewable in the UI

## Blocked by

Slice 10 — Worklog Draft Builder

title: Context budgeter
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Add a budgeter to the Context Assembler that keeps the bundle within the local model's window: per-source caps, prioritizing notes + diff, and summarizing large Confluence pages before inclusion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-source caps are applied so the assembled context fits a configured budget
- [ ] Notes and diff are prioritized over large sources
- [ ] Oversized Confluence pages are summarized before inclusion
- [ ] Assembling oversized inputs no longer overflows the model window

## Blocked by

Slice 16 — Context Assembler (Ticket Work Context)

title: Jira status transition from dashboard
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

From the dashboard the developer changes a ticket's status (e.g., to Doing). Transitions are dynamic: the Jira Client fetches available transitions for the ticket's current workflow state (GET .../transitions), presents them, and applies the chosen one (POST .../transitions with transitionId). No status is hardcoded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Available transitions are fetched for the ticket's current state
- [ ] Selecting a transition applies it via POST and the ticket's status updates
- [ ] Only valid transitions for the current state are offered
- [ ] Transition failures surface a clear error

## Blocked by

Slice 5 — Active ticket selection
close_reason: Implemented getTransitions + applyTransition on JiraClient with full tests, IPC handlers, preload bridge, and transition picker UI on the active ticket

title: Manual worklog -> Tempo submit
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

The developer manually creates a worklog draft (ticket, time, description) held in worklog_draft, reviews it, and on explicit approval the Tempo Client submits it to Tempo. Submission uses the separate Tempo token/host and resolves the numeric Jira issueId (from ticket_cache) and author accountId that Tempo requires.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A manual worklog draft can be created and stored in worklog_draft
- [ ] Submission requires explicit approval (nothing auto-sent)
- [ ] Tempo Client posts the worklog using the separate token/host with issueId + accountId
- [ ] A submitted worklog appears in Tempo; submission errors are surfaced

## Blocked by

Slice 6 — Jira status transition from dashboard

title: Assist: what should I do on this ticket
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

For the active ticket, assemble a minimal context (the Jira ticket fields) and ask the local LLM what needs to be done; show the answer. The developer can also manually pick/paste a specific item as additional context. On-demand only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Assist sends the active ticket's fields to the LLM and shows a grounded answer
- [ ] The developer can manually add/paste extra context for the request
- [ ] The interaction is on-demand (explicit user action)

## Blocked by

Slice 14 — LLM client + health-check + model picker

title: Jira connection + dashboard ticket list
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Using the stored Jira base URL + token (Basic email:token), the Jira Client fetches the developer's assigned tickets in the open sprint (JQL: assignee = currentUser() AND sprint in openSprints()) and the dashboard lists them. The key -> numeric issueId (and summary) is cached in ticket_cache for later use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Jira Client authenticates with Basic email:token and runs a JQL search
- [ ] Dashboard lists my open-sprint assigned tickets
- [ ] ticket_cache stores key -> issueId + summary
- [ ] Auth/connection failures surface a clear error

## Blocked by

Slice 3 — Settings + encrypted secrets
close_reason: JiraClient, ticket_cache, fetchMyOpenSprintTickets, IPC handler jira:getMyOpenTickets implemented with TDD. Dashboard shows open sprint tickets. 31/31 tests pass. UI verified via typecheck+build (Electron launch blocked by WSL2 headless limitation — pre-existing issue).

title: Active ticket selection

## What to build

Read-only Confluence access: the Confluence Client searches pages by CQL and fetches page text for reading inside O.G.A.R. No create or update operations exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CQL search returns matching pages
- [ ] Page text/content can be fetched and displayed
- [ ] No write/create/update path exists (read-only by construction)
- [ ] Uses the stored Confluence token

## What to build

When worklog drafts are built (from sessions/commits), use the LLM to draft each worklog's description from that day's commits and notes for the ticket, so entries are meaningful before submission.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each suggested worklog draft gets an LLM-drafted description from that day's commits + notes
- [ ] Descriptions are editable before approval
- [ ] The described drafts flow into the existing submit + reconcile path

title: LLM client + health-check + model picker
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

The LLM Client targets the OpenAI-compatible API (chat, list models, health) so the local backend is swappable; Ollama is the default. On startup the app pings the endpoint and, if unreachable (e.g., Ollama not started in WSL, or port forwarding dropped after reboot), shows a clear remediation message and a re-check action. The developer picks a model from the locally installed models.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LLM Client calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for chat and model listing
- [ ] Startup health-check detects an unreachable endpoint and shows remediation + re-check (no silent failure)
- [ ] The developer selects a model from /v1/models; the choice persists
- [ ] No external/cloud endpoint is used (local-only)

## Blocked by

Slice 13 — Confluence read (CQL search + page text)

title: Jira comment: draft -> approve -> post
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

From the assembled Ticket Work Context, the LLM drafts a plain-text Jira comment (assist_draft). On explicit approval, the comment is posted to Jira (plain text, e.g., wrapped in a minimal ADF document). Posting errors are surfaced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The LLM drafts a plain-text comment from the assembled context, stored as assist_draft
- [ ] Posting requires explicit approval (nothing auto-posted)
- [ ] An approved comment appears on the Jira ticket
- [ ] Posting failures (auth/network) surface a clear error

## Blocked by

Slice 17 — Context budgeter

title: Worklog reconcile + verify
description:
## Parent

o_g_a_r-lip

## What to build

Add the Worklog Reconciler to the submission path so time is never double-logged. Before submitting, read the day's existing Tempo worklogs for the author and drop drafts that would duplicate them; after submitting, read back and confirm each intended entry appeared, recording per-entry status. Tempo is the source of truth; local status is for UI only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pre-submit: existing Tempo worklogs for author+date are fetched and duplicate drafts are skipped
- [ ] Post-submit: a read-back confirms each intended entry; missing ones are flagged
- [ ] Re-running a submission does not create duplicate worklogs
- [ ] Each draft shows per-entry status (confirmed/failed), not all-or-nothing

## Blocked by

Slice 7 — Manual worklog -> Tempo submit
